finding.claim: Sync verifier with an empty-string or null key skips the empty-key guard and accepts unsigned tokens for any HS* algorithm in the allowlist (fail-open).
finding.source: Unauthenticated client sends header {"alg":"HS256"}, attacker-chosen payload, and an empty signature segment (decoder.js:41 accepts it).
finding.sink: verify() returns the payload as authenticated (verifier.js:426).

trace.note: Type check accepts '' and null because typeof null === 'object'.
if (key && keyType !== 'function') is false for '' or null, so detectPublicKeyAlgorithms and prepareKeyOrSecret never run; the empty-secret guard at verifier.js:38 is never reached.
hasKey = !!key is false and signature is '', so the missingSignature and missingKey checks both pass.
if (signature && ...) is skipped because the signature is empty.
Only remaining check is allowedAlgorithms.includes('HS256'), which is true when algorithms: ['HS256'] is configured.

finding.guards_checked: Explicit algorithms allowlist (passes); hasKey && !signature (not triggered, no key); !hasKey && signature (not triggered, empty signature); empty-key guard (bypassed by line 514). Async path not affected: Buffer.from('') reaches prepareKeyOrSecret and throws. Verified by reading only, not executed.

finding.claim: With caching enabled, tokens without iat get no exp-based cache TTL, so expired tokens are accepted for up to cacheTTL after exp.
finding.source: Holder of a validly signed token without iat (issuer uses noTimestamp: true), verified once before exp.
finding.sink: Cache hit returns the cached payload as valid (verifier.js:374-377).

trace.note: hasIat is false, so cacheValue[2] stays 0.
Max TTL falls back to now + clockTolerance + cacheTTL, not exp.
now <= max still holds after exp, so the cached payload is returned.

finding.guards_checked: Cache must be enabled (verifier.js:580, default off). Signature and exp checked on first verification only. Verified by reading only, not executed.

finding.claim: Claim validators skip absent claims, so allowedAud, allowedIss, allowedSub, allowedNonce and maxAge are bypassed when the claim is missing unless requiredClaims is set.
finding.source: Holder of a validly signed token that omits aud/iss, where the same key is shared across audiences.
finding.sink: verify() accepts the token for a service it was not issued for (verifier.js:426).

trace.note: if (!(claim in payload)) continue skips the validator.
requiredClaims check is opt-in and not applied by default.
allowedAud/allowedIss/allowedSub/allowedNonce validators are only added when configured.

finding.guards_checked: Signature (valid). requiredClaims (not configured by default). Design concern; needs shared key and an issuer that omits the claim. Verified by reading only.

finding.claim: Non-TokenError exceptions are cached and later returned as a successful payload.
finding.source: Validly signed token without iat whose nbf or exp is outside the Date range, or the empty-key bypass in F1.
finding.sink: handleCachedResult returns the cached Error object as the payload (verifier.js:153, 377).

trace.note: validateClaimDateValue calls new Date(adjusted).toISOString(), which throws RangeError for out-of-range values.
Sync catch calls cacheSet with a non-TokenError, which falls through to the success branch.
Without iat, min is 0 and max is maxTTL, so the entry is returned on the next call.

finding.guards_checked: cacheSet special-cases only TokenError. Requires signed out-of-range claims or F1. Low severity. Verified by reading only.

finding.claim: Async complete mode returns input: token (full token including signature) instead of the signing input that sync mode returns.
finding.source: Caller using complete: true in async mode.
finding.sink: Application code that re-verifies the signature using the returned input.

trace.note: Sync mode returns input from the decoder (header.payload).
Async mode returns input: token instead.

finding.guards_checked: Fail-closed for the library itself. Logic inconsistency, low severity. Verified by reading only.

finding.claim: Non-canonical base64url signature segments are accepted, so one signature has many token strings.
finding.source: Any client that alters unused low bits of the last signature character.
finding.sink: Application-level replay or denylists keyed on the token string; signature check itself is unaffected.

trace.note: BASE64URL_RE checks only the alphabet, not canonical trailing bits.
Signature segment passes the check as-is.
Buffer.from(signature, 'base64') ignores the unused low bits.
Comment claims the signature is canonical, which is not enforced.

finding.guards_checked: HMAC compared with timingSafeEqual (crypto.js:391). Only token-string-keyed controls are affected. Low severity. Verified by reading only.
